comments.author: @lauriebutler4115
comments.text: Of course teachers want to work.  They just don’t want to have to do battle everyday. They want to come to work, have a great day teaching kids and feel like they are making progress. These teachers are giving up steady, generally well paying jobs with insurance and benefits because the children in so many of these inner city and poverty stricken schools are without limits, have no manners, are disrespectful and sometimes violent  to everyone and just make teaching impossible. The entire day is filled with behavior issues and repetition of everthing. It’s society, poverty, entitlement, children raising children, uneducated parents raising uneducated children, no books or reading in the homes, no limits, addiction to cell phones and computers and he inability to concentrate on anything ….on and on.   Great teachers are leaving those dangerous public schools for suburban, private and parochial schools where the children come to school more prepared, are generally  polite, respectful and ready to learn.  That means teachers sacrifice better salaries and benefits for lower pay and  a better working environment in private schools or public schools in affluent suburbs. .   If a child is rude and disrespectful or violent at a private school he can be kicked out……….they either conform to the rules or go elsewhere.   Many of these schools only take a certain level of student and require testing before admission. Can’t do that in the public schools…..they have to accept all students in their district including those with problems and try to survive.   Teachers can’t fix the problems of society, poverty and culture but they have to deal with it. Reading starts in the home.  If the parent can’t read……..the kids start off at an extreme disadvantage.   I don’t know what the answer is, but teachers can’t fix the world!  In order to keep great teachers in these schools they need support from parents and administrators to stop or remove the behavior problems and violent students and parents and they need time to plan and prepare.  Teachers need to be well paid. The job is hard and requires continual education to maintain licensure which comes out of their pocket.
